# Locality Guide: Triesen, Liechtenstein (1740s)

## Jurisdiction & Background

Triesen is a municipality in the southern Principality of Liechtenstein, bordered by Austria (Vorarlberg) to the east and Switzerland (Graubünden/St. Gallen) to the west. In 1743 Liechtenstein was a principality within the Holy Roman Empire; it became fully sovereign in 1806. No boundary changes affected Triesen's ecclesiastical jurisdiction for this period. Records are organised at the local municipality (Gemeinde) level. Population of all Liechtenstein c.1800: ~5,802 (country-level Gapminder estimate).

## Primary Source for 1743: Catholic Church Records

Civil registration did not begin until **1878** (births/marriages/deaths) and **1789** (family registers) — both postdate the 1743 christening. The sole contemporary source is the **Catholic parish register**.

| Record Set | Coverage | Access | Digitisation Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Triesen Kirchenbuch, 1638–1916 | Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations | FS catalog #115845 — microfilmed; volume_search returned 0 results; may require FamilySearch Center | Browse-only (microfilm) |
| Liechtenstein, Births & Baptisms, 1650–1875 (FS coll. 1708589) | Country-wide partial index | Free at FamilySearch; also Ancestry ($), MyHeritage ($), Findmypast ($) | Partial index + images — Legacy Collection |

**Critical caveat:** Collection 1708589 is a Legacy Collection — incomplete for every place and time period. FamilySearch has ~468 indexed birth records for all of Liechtenstein 1700–1750. A hit must be verified against the original; a miss does not prove absence.

## Other Record Types

- Familienbücher (Family Registers), Triesen Standesamt, 1794–1956 — FS catalog #103425, microfilm. Begins 1794; may contain retrospective family data but 1743 predates this series.
- Liechtenstein State Archives (Landesarchiv, Vaduz) — court, land, and probate records; no 18th-century online access.
- Historischer Verein für das Fürstentum Liechtenstein: https://www.lub.li/

## Key Quirks

1. Index is incomplete — a miss is not proof of absence; always check the original Kirchenbuch.
2. Kirchenbuch (1638–1916) appears microfilm-only; may require a FamilySearch Center visit.
3. Records written in Latin (Catholic); German Genealogical Word List and Latin Genealogical Word List essential.
4. Population coverage ~50% before 1800 — significant gaps in the indexed portion.
5. Triesen borders Austria (Vorarlberg) and Switzerland — search neighboring parishes if Triesen records are silent.

**Locality Guide: Triesen, Liechtenstein — 1740s**

## Jurisdiction & Background

Triesen is a municipality in the southern Principality of Liechtenstein, bordered by Austria (Vorarlberg) to the east and Switzerland (Graubünden/St. Gallen) to the west. In 1743 Liechtenstein was a principality within the Holy Roman Empire — it became fully sovereign in 1806. No boundary changes affected Triesen's ecclesiastical jurisdiction for this period. Records are organised at the local municipality (Gemeinde) level. Population of all Liechtenstein c.1800: ~5,802 (country estimate, Gapminder).

---

## Primary Source for 1743: Catholic Church Records

Civil registration did not begin until **1878** (births/marriages/deaths) and **1789** (family registers) — both postdate the 1743 christening entirely. The sole contemporary source is the **Catholic parish register**.

| Triesen Kirchenbuch, 1638–1916 | Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations | FamilySearch catalog [#115845](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/115845) — microfilmed; `volume_search` returned 0 results, so digitised online browsing not confirmed; may require a FamilySearch Center visit | Browse-only (microfilm); digitisation status unclear |

[1708589](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1708589)) | Country-wide partial index; 34,173 index entries with images | Free at FamilySearch; also Ancestry ($), MyHeritage ($), Findmypast ($) | **Partial index + images — Legacy Collection** |

**Critical caveat:** Collection 1708589 is a **Legacy Collection** — assembled from various sources (including the IGI), no further records will be added, and the index is explicitly incomplete for every place and time period. FamilySearch counts only ~468 indexed birth records for all of Liechtenstein 1700–1750. A hit must be verified against the original register; a miss does **not** prove absence.

---

## Other Record Types (Background / Secondary)

- **Familienbücher (Family Registers), Triesen Standesamt, 1794–1956** — catalog [#103425](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/103425), microfilm. Begins 1794 — may contain retrospective family data, but the 1743 event predates this series.
- **State Archives (Liechtensteinisches Landesarchiv, Vaduz)** — holds court, land, and probate records; no 18th-century online access. Contact for original research.
- **Historischer Verein für das Fürstentum Liechtenstein**: https://www.lub.li/ — images of historical documents.

---

1. The FamilySearch births index (1708589) is incomplete — a miss is not proof of absence; always check the original Kirchenbuch.
2. Church records for Triesen (Kirchenbuch 1638–1916) appear microfilm-only as of this survey (`volume_search` returned 0 results) — access may require a FamilySearch Center or ordering the film.

Records are written in **Latin** (Catholic) with German surname/place elements; a [Latin Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Latin_Genealogical_Word_List) and [German Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/German_Genealogical_Word_List) are essential.

6. The FamilySearch Wiki does not have a `Liechtenstein_Vital_Records` page; civil registration dates (1878 / 1789) are sourced from the [Liechtenstein Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Liechtenstein_Civil_Registration) and [Triesen Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Triesen,_Liechtenstein_Genealogy) wiki pages.
